authors: Brill, Chaudhari, Polak, Rawat, Pandey, Bhatt, Dholakia, Murali

mcqs.q: In the Indian dog-ownership survey, how did dog-owning household prevalence in Gujarat compare with Tamil Nadu?
mcqs.e: Gujarat settlements had significantly fewer dog-owning households than Tamil Nadu.

mcqs.q: Across settlements, what were the relative sterilisation and rabies-vaccination proportions of owned dogs?
mcqs.e: Sterilisation was typically low while rabies vaccination was high.

mcqs.q: Dog ownership was most associated with which household characteristic?
mcqs.e: Ownership was more common in higher-socioeconomic households.

authors: Chaudhari, Brill, Chakravarti, Drees, Verma, Avinash, Jha, Langain, Bhatt, Kumar, Choudhary, Singh, Chandra, Murali, Polak

mcqs.q: Why does HSIApps emphasise returning a sterilised street dog to its exact capture location?
o: Because territorial dogs face welfare risks and postoperative complications if misplaced
mcqs.e: Street dogs are territorial; misplacement risks welfare problems and postoperative complications including death.

mcqs.q: What type of tool is HSIApps?
mcqs.e: HSIApps is a mobile phone-based data-collection application.

mcqs.q: How is sterilisation characterised for street-dog population control?
o: One of the most humane and effective methods
mcqs.e: Sterilisation is described as among the most humane and effective population-control methods.

mcqs.q: Which pathogen, detected only by the university laboratory, was implicated as substantially involved in the outbreak?
mcqs.e: Only the university lab detected canine pneumovirus, implicated as substantially involved.

mcqs.q: The CIRDC outbreak resolved within about one month after which interventions?
o: Clean break procedures, limiting intake, and deep cleaning
mcqs.e: Resolution followed clean break procedures, limiting incoming dogs, and a deep clean.

mcqs.q: How many fatalities occurred in the outbreak?
mcqs.e: The outbreak comprised eight fatalities among over 100 cases.

authors: Jaffey, Lappin, Ringold, Kriesler, Bradley-Siemens, Hawley, Sun, Blakeman, Mayer

mcqs.q: How did serum 25(OH)D compare in shelter dogs with CIRDC signs versus apparently healthy shelter dogs?
mcqs.e: Dogs with CIRDC signs had significantly lower serum 25(OH)D.

mcqs.q: Was serum 25(OH)D concentration associated with duration of time in the shelter?
mcqs.e: 25(OH)D was not associated with time spent in the shelter.

mcqs.q: How did shelter dogs' 25(OH)D compare with nonshelter control dogs?
mcqs.e: Shelter dog 25(OH)D did not differ significantly from controls.

authors: Hawes, Hupe, Winczewski, Elting, Arrington, Newbury, Morris

mcqs.q: The urban Pets for Life intervention community showed what compared with the non-intervention urban site?
o: Lower overall access to pet care
Higher overall access to pet care
mcqs.e: The intervention community had higher overall measured access to pet care.

mcqs.q: Which specific access measures were higher in the intervention community?
mcqs.e: Access to affordable care and providers offering payment options was higher.

mcqs.q: What does the study conclude about community-based animal welfare programming?
o: It has no effect on access
It can increase perceptions of access to pet support services
mcqs.e: Such programming has potential to increase perceptions of access to pet support services.

authors: Dines, Kellihan, Allen, Loynachan, Bochsler, Newbury

mcqs.q: How were the two puppies that died suddenly diagnosed?
mcqs.e: Both were diagnosed with parvoviral myocarditis at necropsy.

mcqs.q: What were the cardiac diagnostic results of the seven screened surviving puppies?
o: All normal, with dogs alive and thriving at 5 years
mcqs.e: All seven had normal echo/ECG/troponin and were alive and thriving at 5 years.

mcqs.q: What does the report conclude about outcomes for littermates of parvoviral myocarditis puppies?
mcqs.e: Outcomes are variable and need not be grave; cardiac diagnostics aid prognosis.

mcqs.q: Estimated survival for obtunded/lateral pyometra patients treated at HQHVSN clinics was approximately?
mcqs.e: Obtunded/lateral patients had an estimated ~38% survival.

mcqs.q: How did HQHVSN pyometra treatment fees compare with private practice and emergency hospitals?
mcqs.e: HQHVSN fees (~$200 dog/$125 cat) were much lower than private/ER estimates.

mcqs.q: What proportion of HQHVSN clinics were willing to treat nonincidental pyometra at least sometimes?
mcqs.e: Most clinics (86%) were willing to treat nonincidental pyometra at least sometimes.

authors: Beall, Buch, Clark, Estrada, Rakitin, Hamman, Frenden, Jefferson, Amirian, Levy

mcqs.q: Median survival of high-positive FeLV cats from enrollment was approximately?
mcqs.e: High-positive cats had a median survival of 1.37 years.

mcqs.q: What was the survival of low-positive FeLV cats over the four-year study?
mcqs.e: Most low-positive cats (93.1%) remained alive.

mcqs.q: Quantitative p27 antigen concentration and proviral DNA load were highly correlated with?
mcqs.e: Both quantitative measures correlated highly with survival times.

authors: van der Laan, Vinke, van der Borg, Arndt

mcqs.q: How did shelter dogs' nocturnal activity change from the first nights to night 12?
mcqs.e: Nocturnal activity was higher in the first nights and decreased by night 12.

mcqs.q: Did the study find a 'first-night effect' on sleep?
mcqs.e: No first-night effect was found; activity did not differ between nights 1 and 2.

mcqs.q: How did body weight change between intake and the two-week habituation period?
mcqs.e: Dogs lost on average about 5% of body weight.

authors: Powell, Reinhard, Satriale, Morris, Serpell, Watson

mcqs.q: What were the most common reasons for adoption return?
o: Behavioral issues and incompatibility with existing pets
mcqs.e: Behavioral issues and incompatibility with existing pets were most common.

mcqs.q: Which group had the greatest odds of post-adoption return?
mcqs.e: Adult dogs had the greatest odds of return (OR 3.40).

mcqs.q: Pit bull-type breeds were more likely to experience which outcomes?
mcqs.e: Pit bull-type breeds were returned multiple times and euthanized post-return more often.

authors: Gunter, Gilchrist, Blade, Barber, Feuerbacher, Platzer, Wynne

mcqs.q: What happened to dogs' cortisol:creatinine ratios on the afternoon of the 2.5-hour outing?
o: Significantly higher, returning to baseline the next day
mcqs.e: Cortisol was higher during the intervention afternoon but returned to baseline the following day.

mcqs.q: What is the study's main conclusion about brief outings versus temporary fostering?
o: Short outings do not confer the same stress-reduction benefits
mcqs.e: Short-term outings did not provide the stress reduction previously shown with temporary fostering.

mcqs.q: How did physical activity change during the outing?
o: High activity increased while low activity decreased
mcqs.e: High activity increased and low activity decreased during the outings.

journal: Journal of Applied Animal Welfare Science

mcqs.q: Which factors were significantly associated with lower daily weight gain in shelter kittens?
mcqs.e: Lethargy and female sex were significantly associated with lower daily weight gain.

mcqs.q: How did shelter/foster kittens' average daily weight gain compare with catteries and laboratories?
mcqs.e: Average daily weight gain was higher than reported in catteries and labs.

mcqs.q: What was the kitten mortality rate in the study?
mcqs.e: Five kittens (2.5%) died or were euthanized.
